correctness.rationale: Exact inversion of isotone maps is classified by independent kernel-transversal and image-cut conditions. Balanced integer compositions establish fixed-rank maxima; integer-break bounds and a two-case residue-three argument prove the global optimum, all equality ranks, and enumerations. The squared binomial rankwise inverse-pair law follows from two coefficient extractions. Direct exhaustive composition through n=6 and independently computed rank bounds through n=500 agree, but finite checks alone are not relied on as proof.

The local crossed-square incidence and kernel/image parametrization are explicitly prior to the current result. value.rationale: Recent balanced-weighting work solves existence of permutation matchings but identifies nonregular inverse neighborhoods as the main obstacle. The theorem quantifies their sharp all-dimensional degree heterogeneity, exact maximizing ranks, numbers of maximizers, and all rankwise edges. The recurrence with growth base 9^(1/3) is structural and answers a naturally motivated extremal inverse-graph question, not an arbitrary finite table or a rephrasing of matching existence.
